# IFN-γ IN CANCER PATIENTS

pharmacokinetic studies indicate that this agent was altered before reaching the bloodstream, resulting in partial loss of antiviral activity. These data suggest that further investigations with i.m. injections as well as prolonged i.v. infusions of IFN-γ are warranted. This study will form the framework for future Phase I, II, and III evaluations of the role of rIFN-γ in the therapy of human viral, microbial, and malignant diseases.
